title: Gujarat horror: PG girl raped on terrace; guard arrested
content: A security guard allegedly raped a 22-year-old student on a society terrace late Saturday.  The accused, Dharm Singh, was arrested early Sunday morning by Anandnagar police.  He had approached the student with sexual intentions and assaulted her when she refused.  The woman was rescued by residents after the guard fled with her phone.  Police are investigating the incident and the guard's background.

title: 19 days in jail, 'stole' police chair and deportation: Japanese student’s Bengaluru story
content: A Japanese student recently secured compensation after spending nineteen unjust days in custody. In a bizarre twist, he tried to evade repatriation by pilfering a police chair, aiming to extend his time in India. This incident arose from conflicts at an English academy and alleged bribery claims. The human rights commission ruled in his favor, underscoring the complexities of his legal and immigration battles in Bengaluru.

title: Microsoft warns travellers: Hotel Wi-Fi can expose passwords, audio and video
content: Microsoft has issued a warning for travelers about potential cyberattacks targeting hotel Wi-Fi networks. The CaptiveCrunch campaign, linked to group Storm-2945, leads users to fraudulent portals. Victims might unconsciously download harmful files or disclose sensitive information. These threats are focused on compromising Microsoft 365 accounts and gaining unauthorized network access. For safety, travelers are advised to utilize cellular hotspots and to disregard any unexpected pop-up notifications.

title: ‘Not taking up the position’: Why Laxman turned down head coach job after Dravid
content: VVS Laxman has revealed why he turned down the India head coach role after Rahul Dravid’s tenure ended in 2024. Approached by the BCCI following India’s T20 World Cup triumph under Dravid, Laxman opted to continue at the Centre of Excellence, citing family considerations and his desire to develop the facility.

title: At 5, Fateh Singh Gill is a world martial arts champion
content: At just five years old, Fateh Singh Gill from Amritsar has made waves on the international martial arts scene, winning gold at the World Martial Art Games in Thailand on skates. His impressive journey started at two, where his parents recognized his innate talent and provided steadfast support. They encourage children to explore their natural capabilities, allowing them to shine on their chosen paths.

title: Elon Musk's preferred state halts data centre approvals; says 'prove' this first
content: In response to mounting concerns about the swift expansion of data centers, Texas Governor Greg Abbott has placed a temporary hold on new approvals for these facilities. Regulators are set to carry out an extensive audit, requiring developers to demonstrate their water and electricity demands prior to gaining grid access. This measure is aimed at ensuring the well-being and safety of Texans amidst this rapid growth.

title: Houston man’s solo trash cleanups grow into 100-volunteer movement
content: A Houston resident's initiative to clean up neglected areas has blossomed into a vibrant volunteer movement. With one hundred dedicated individuals now on board, their mission is to remove illegally dumped waste. Collaborating with local organizations and harnessing the power of social media, city officials and law enforcement are boosting efforts to tackle this pressing issue, ultimately enhancing the community's aesthetics and the well-being of its residents.

title: Sundar Pichai's letter to Google staff on AI leadership change: 'We'll keep moving'
content: Google DeepMind announces significant leadership changes to advance its AI strategy. Demis Hassabis will chair Google DeepMind and become Chief Scientist of Alphabet. Jeff Dean departs after 27 years to launch a new public benefit corporation. Koray Kavukcuoglu will now lead Gemini model development and frontier AI research. These shifts aim to accelerate artificial general intelligence and scientific breakthroughs.

title: Sarfaraz Khan's first reaction after India call-up for Sri Lanka Test series
content: Sarfaraz Khan has been added to India's Test squad for the Sri Lanka series. He replaces Sai Sudharsan, who is recovering from a toe injury. This marks a significant moment for the batter after a long wait. The upcoming series is crucial for India's World Test Championship final hopes. India will play two Test matches against Sri Lanka starting August 15.

title: Govt may be going slow on FCRA to woo DMK, NCP(SP) for delimitation
content: As Parliament approaches its closing week, the FCRA amendment bill is notably absent from Monday's Lok Sabha agenda, signaling a possible political strategy from the government. The legislation's contentious nature is drawing connections to the pending delimitation exercise. Opposition groups, including DMK and NCP(SP), have raised alarms over its provisions. It seems the government wishes to foster a detailed discussion to address these criticisms.

title: 'Yuvraj asked me to stand on the chair': Shami's dressing room experience
content: Mohammed Shami shared his initial nervousness upon joining the Indian cricket team. He recalled Yuvraj Singh asking him to speak to the team during a meeting. Shami also identified Shikhar Dhawan as the team's funniest player. Dhawan often lifted the mood even after India suffered a defeat. These anecdotes highlight the camaraderie within the Indian dressing room.

title: LeT operative linked to 26/11 Mumbai attacks dies in Pak; poisoning suspected
content: In a puzzling incident, a prominent Lashkar-e-Taiba member, Qari Saeed Abdul Aziz, was found dead in Islamabad on August 8. Known for his role in orchestrating the 26/11 Mumbai attacks, Aziz collapsed near a mosque after a meal at an unfamiliar restaurant. While the exact cause of death is still being investigated, the possibility of poisoning has not been ruled out, prompting close scrutiny from regional intelligence.

title: Jharkhand students to gherao state assembly today as talks fail
content: Job aspirants in Ranchi are resolute in staging an assembly gherao, disregarding governmental entreaties and discussions. The impasse continues, driven by demands for a CBI investigation and the annulment of the JSSC-CGL 2024 exam. Tensions escalated after three JPSC members resigned before facing CID questioning. With police presence heightened, prohibitive orders are enforced near the assembly to safeguard public order during these tumultuous protests.

title: Oil price today: Brent crude jumps over 1% as traders await Hormuz reopening
content: On Monday, oil prices surged amid ongoing uncertainty surrounding the reopening of the Hormuz Strait. While Iran and Oman are closing in on an agreement for a shipping lane, Iran's demands for concessions from the U.S. linger. Adding to market tensions, Houthi rebels targeted Saudi Aramco's Jazan refinery, igniting a fire, along with numerous attacks in the Red Sea and Gulf of Aden, raising serious concerns about oil shipment security.

title: Hyderabad's NALSAR students oppose CJI Surya Kant as convocation chief guest
content: NALSAR students have requested the university reconsider inviting Chief Justice Surya Kant as chief guest.  They cited concerns over his reported remarks during a recent court hearing.  Students submitted multiple representations to the administration expressing their objections.  These students feel the choice conflicts with university values and constitutional principles.  The university administration has not yet responded to the students' concerns.

title: Turbulent AI flight’s pilot dope test ‘not negative’, sent for confirmation: Govt
content: Following a serious incident involving altitude loss on an Air India flight, the pilot was subjected to a dope screening test. The results were not definitively negative, thereby calling for additional confirmatory tests. As a result, seventeen passengers and crew members were hospitalized. In response, the aviation ministry has initiated an investigation and temporarily removed both pilots from their flying duties until the inquiry concludes.

title: Iran appoints former IRGC chief as top security official amid Hormuz reopening talks
content: Iran has named Mohsen Rezaei as the head of its Supreme National Security Council, following the resignation of Mohammad Bagher Zolghadr. This leadership transformation unfolds as discussions surrounding the reopening of the Strait of Hormuz are underway. With his vast experience as a former Revolutionary Guard commander, Rezaei’s appointment marks a noteworthy adjustment in Iran’s national security landscape.

title: Thalapathy Vijay's 'Jana Nayagan' jumps 41.2% on Day 18, adds Rs 3.60 cr
content: Jana Nayagan saw a significant box office jump on its third Sunday. The film's India net collection increased by 41.2 percent from Saturday. Its total India net collection has now reached Rs 192.30 crore. Worldwide gross collection for Jana Nayagan has crossed Rs 317 crore. The Tamil version recorded strong occupancy across multiple shows.

title: 2 years after RG Kar horror, Bengal chief minister announces inquiry panel
content: West Bengal government will establish an inquiry commission for the RG Kar rape-murder case. Police will also investigate the hurried cremation of the trainee doctor, which occurred two years ago. This decision follows a request from the victim's mother, who is now a BJP MLA. The state government aims to ensure justice and punish all responsible individuals. Annual programs will be organized to mark Abhaya Day, commemorating the victim.

title: Russia proposes direct rail link to India to bypass Bosphorus & Hormuz straits
content: Russia has proposed a direct rail corridor to connect to the Indian Ocean, aiming to circumvent the perilous straits. This ambitious route would pass through Turkmenistan, Iran, Afghanistan, and Pakistan. However, experts highlight significant logistical and financial hurdles. For New Delhi, gaining Pakistan's commitment to security cooperation is essential. If realized, this corridor might provide a vital overland freight option to reduce reliance on maritime routes.

title: ED director Rahul Navin's tenure extended by a year
content: Rahul Navin received a one-year extension as ED director, which ends his fixed tenure. His service is now extended until August 2027, including post-superannuation service. Navin's tenure began in September 2023 and was appointed ED director in August 2024. He has established a roadmap for completing probes and auctioning attached properties. This roadmap aims to return assets to rightful claimants and fraud victims.

title: JNU cancels event on Umar Khalid’s book, says full information not disclosed
content: Jawaharlal Nehru University has canceled a student-organized discussion on Umar Khalid's work, citing a lack of full disclosure regarding event details. Planned for International Day of the World’s Indigenous Peoples, the JNU Students’ Union announced they would continue the discussion outside the venue. The Teachers’ Association criticized this cancellation as an infringement on academic freedom and expression.

title: PMAY-Urban: Govt says 1.25 crore houses sanctioned, 1 crore delivered
content: The Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana-Urban has granted over 1.25 crore homes, with more than one crore completed to date. Notably, one crore of those houses were designated for women beneficiaries nationwide. Recently, the scheme approved an additional 2.09 lakh homes for economically weaker section families, bringing the total under PMAY-U 2.0 to over 18.38 lakh houses. The government is diligently assessing the scheme's execution and fund use across various states.

title: Rahul targets Shah over silence on Delhi Police action; cites student anguish
content: Rahul Gandhi has raised concerns regarding Home Minister Amit Shah's muted response to police actions against students protesting at Jantar Mantar over paper leaks. Jairam Ramesh reminded the minister of his silence during a previous security incident in Parliament, emphasizing the need for accountability as the monsoon session nears its conclusion, with opposition members urging the government to address the youth's grievances.

title: India among top nations in quantum technology, says science min Jitendra Singh
content: India is now at par with global leaders in advanced technology and manufacturing.  Technology and artificial intelligence have significantly improved access to opportunities and education.  Chandrayaan's discovery of water molecules on the Moon showcases India's specific capabilities.  Opening the space and nuclear sectors to private companies has spurred rapid expansion.  This progress indicates a fast pace in both manufacturing and technological development.

title: ED charges against RCom, Reliance Infra in 40k crore bank fraud
content: The Enforcement Directorate has formally charged Reliance Communications and Reliance Infrastructure with serious financial offenses, including money laundering involving over forty thousand crore rupees in misappropriated bank funds. The allegations indicate substantial financial misconduct by both companies and related individuals. The agency is pursuing the confiscation of properties worth more than eight thousand crore rupees, stemming from a deliberate scheme to misdirect public funds from vital infrastructure projects.

title: 7 of 25 high courts without CJs, collegium recommends names for just four
content: The Supreme Court collegium recommended four judges for High Court Chief Justice positions.  These appointments aim to fill vacancies in key High Courts across India.  The collegium also approved transfers of two judges from Orissa High Court.  Orissa High Court faces a significant shortage of judges, impacting its functioning.  No representation from Orissa High Court has been appointed to the Supreme Court in eight years.

title: One crore homes completed and delivered under PM scheme: Government
content: Since the inception of the Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojna, over one crore urban houses have been built, representing a significant achievement in housing development. Since 2015, 1.25 crore houses have gained approval, with nearly one crore allocated to women. Furthermore, PMAY-Urban 2.0 introduced over 2.09 lakh houses for EWS families, while 1.4 lakh homes were sanctioned for pucca construction under the Beneficiary Led Construction scheme.

title: Recent rain has little impact on national monsoon deficit
content: Recent rains have brought relief to Delhi, Haryana, and eastern Rajasthan, yet the national monsoon deficit persists. States like Bihar and Punjab continue to struggle with below-average rainfall. While the sowing of Kharif crops is nearly finalized across the nation, August's rainfall may enhance water reservoirs for hydropower and upcoming planting seasons, with a low-pressure area potentially raising precipitation levels in eastern India shortly.

title: Indian, US navies kick off 5-day specialised diving, EOD exercise in Kochi
content: In a significant show of unity, the Indian and US navies will engage in a five-day explosive ordnance disposal drill in Kochi. This advanced training initiative aims to bolster interoperability and foster teamwork between the participating units. The event will encompass expert discussions, shared training techniques, and practical exercises. This marks the eighth edition of their cooperative training, emphasizing a mutual focus on enhancing maritime security operations.

title: Op Sindoor showed India will go to any extent to protect its citizens: Defence min
content: Defence minister Rajnath Singh lauded Operation Sindoor for protecting citizens and sending a strong global message. He compared the operation's courage to the compassion shown at a large blood donation camp. Around one thousand wrestlers and athletes from Maharashtra donated blood at the Delhi Cantt event. Singh emphasized blood donation as a vital contribution, calling it 'Jivandan' and 'Mahadan'.

title: Police search 26 locations tied to banned Jamaat-e-Islami J&K
content: Authorities conducted extensive searches at twenty-six locations in Sopore, north Kashmir, specifically targeting the premises of Jamaat-e-Islami J&K. Critical documents and electronic devices were seized amid an investigation into the organization’s potential ties to terrorism. This operation is part of an intensified effort in the area following the tragic shooting of a police officer, highlighting ongoing security threats posed by the banned group.

title: Search ops involving Indian Navy for 3 missing fishermen continue in Kerala
content: The Indian Navy's search for three missing fishermen continues into its tenth day.  Divers are utilizing portable SONAR to enhance underwater surveillance capabilities.  INS Kalpeni joined the operation, sailing from Kochi to aid the search efforts.  The search initially focused on Gautam Krishna, who went missing off the Neendakara coast.  The operation is ongoing off the Kollam and Thiruvananthapuram coasts.
